Subject: MAP: final evaluation runway & fallbacks for deployment-mode + region split

Claire / Stethix team —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is an updated MAP workbook (Stethix_MAP_v3.xlsx) with three small changes we discussed: a tightened pilot acceptance criterion, explicit latency SLOs for the hosted demo, and the proposed rollback/fallback policy between Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

As a quick summary, propose the following runway for the evaluation and close: 
- Week of Nov 30: Hosted pilot in us-west for the clinician search flow (3-day traffic window).
- Week of Dec 7: Performance/throughput test against Dedicated config (reserved pool) for the heavier batch inference path.
- Week of Dec 14: Security evidence & Private environment scoping (if firm needs PHI segregation).

Asks from your side this week: 
1) Confirm that procurement can sign the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and target the Dec 15 signature gate.
2) Tell us which of the two production regions you prefer (us-west vs us-east) for initial go-live. If you need a geo split we can present cost+latency tradeoffs.
3) Any additional SOC2 evidence items your security team needs ahead of the Private scoping call.

Attachments: Stethix_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP workbook) — Marcus included the acceptance criteria and owner assignments.

I'll follow up with a short readout with ops owners (Dylan + Laura) once you confirm the region preference.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Claire —

Quick answers to the items you called out: 

1) Pricing lines: added a concise table to Stethix_MAP_v3.xlsx under tab 'Commercial' with per-token hosted rates (pilot/production tiers) and two Dedicated commit bands (monthly 2k GPU-hours, 5k GPU-hours). Priya — please confirm values in the sheet match the commercial offer.

2) Latency SLOs (us-west, median payload ~1.2k tokens, single-stream inference): 
- Hosted (standard tier): target 95th = 420ms (warm cache), typical cold-start tail to 800ms on multi-tenant noisy periods.
- Dedicated (reserved pool, pinned capacity): target 95th = 180–220ms (more predictable tail), sustained throughput is better for batch workloads.

Cache/warmup note: the clinician-search flow benefits strongly from prefix/KV caching—if pilot traffic exercises the same prefixes the warmup looks realistic. For safety on the pilot gate we're recommending a 3-day window with synthetic replay of the top-20 prefixes to accelerate cache residency. That step is noted in the MAP acceptance checklist.

3) SOC2 evidence: attached SOC2_evidence.pdf with our summary of control artifacts. If Security asks for anything specific (e.g., KMS key rotation logs, HSM attestation), we can provide the redacted extracts.

4) Fallbacks & rollout: our recommended operational sequence in case of degradation — Hosted -> Dedicated (same region) -> Private (if policy-required). The MAP includes a canary policy and a fallback SLA credit schedule.

DocuSign link to the MAP summary & commercial appendix (for procurement to review & sign): https://docusign.com/stethix/redwood-deal-187

I'll be on the Private scoping call next Thursday if needed.

—Marcus

Claire / procurement team —

Following Marcus' answers and the attached evidence, here's a short mutual-action plan we propose and owners to keep the timeline tight so we can hit a Dec 15 signature: 

Milestones (owners):
- Nov 24: Region decision confirmed (Stethix — Claire / procurement).
- Nov 29: Hosted pilot kickoff in us-west + synthetic-prefix replay (Redwood — Dylan).
- Dec 7: Dedicated perf run + throughput validation (Redwood — Marcus; Stethix Engineering observing).
- Dec 10: Security artifacts final (Stethix Security acceptance) (Redwood — Laura).
- Dec 15: Contract signature (Procurement).

Risks & mitigations: 
- If region undecided by Nov 24 we will run a dual-region smoke in parallel but that adds ~48 hours to the pilot and may push the Dec 15 target.
- If SOC2 extracts require additional redaction steps we will provide a sealed evidence package and run the Private scoping call the week of Dec 14.

Please confirm the Nov 24 region preference and whether procurement needs any other commercial details prior to DocuSign. If all looks good we'll lock the MAP and I will send the DocuSign envelope to procurement@stethix.com tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
